title: Ordinary unbounded derived scalar extension intertwines signed line tensor and evaluation
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme, and work on its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Let $R_0\xrightarrow{r_{10}}R_1\xrightarrow{r_{21}}R_2$ be sheaves of commutative rings, and put $r_{20}=r_{21}r_{10}$. Use module sheaves and their unbounded derived categories $D(R_i)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $L_i$ be $R_i$-module sheaves locally isomorphic to $R_i$, with isomorphisms $b_{ji}:L_i\otimes_{R_i}R_j\cong L_j$ satisfying $b_{20}=b_{21}(b_{10}\otimes1)$ under reassociation. For identity coefficient maps use the multiplication datum $b_{ii}$. Define $M_{i,m}=L_i^{[m]}$ for $m\in\mathbf Z$ by $L_i^{[0]}=R_i$, $L_i^{[m]}=L_i^{\otimes m}$ for $m>0$, and $L_i^{[-m]}=\mathcal Hom_{R_i}(L_i^{[m]},R_i)$ for $m>0$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, def-pur-sheaf-hom]. Let $b_{ji,m}$ be the signed-power scalar comparisons normalized by tensor powers and dual evaluation [lem-pur-signed-line-scalar-tensor-tower]. Put $T_{i,m}(K)=K\otimes^L_{R_i}M_{i,m}$ and $B_{ji}(K)=K\otimes^L_{R_i}R_j$ using K-flat derived tensor [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent, lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings].

Every $M_{i,m}$ is locally free of rank one; $T_{i,m}$ is induced by the exact additive termwise tensor functor on all unbounded complexes, with inverse $T_{i,-m}$ and evaluation $\epsilon_{i,m}:T_{i,-m}T_{i,m}\cong1$ given by actual sheaf evaluation. There are natural isomorphisms $\bar\beta_{ji,m}:B_{ji}T_{i,m}\cong T_{j,m}B_{ji}$. On a flat-term K-flat representative $P$ [def-pc-kflat-complex], $P\otimes M_{i,m}$ and $P\otimes R_j$ are again flat-term K-flat, and $\bar\beta$ is represented by the sheafified balanced chain isomorphism
$$((p\otimes l)\otimes s)\longmapsto(p\otimes s)\otimes b_{ji,m}(l\otimes1).$$
Its inverse is tensor reassociation followed by $b_{ji,m}^{-1}$; its localization is independent of $P$, including naturality for arbitrary derived morphisms. Write $d_K:B_{21}B_{10}K\cong B_{20}K$ for the ordinary associator with formula $(p\otimes s)\otimes t\mapsto p\otimes r_{21}(s)t$ [lem-sfb-successive-derived-quotient-normalization]. Then
$$T_{2,m}(d_K)\circ\bar\beta_{21,m,B_{10}K}\circ B_{21}(\bar\beta_{10,m,K})=\bar\beta_{20,m,K}\circ d_{T_{0,m}K},$$
$$\epsilon_{j,m,B_{ji}K}\circ T_{j,-m}(\bar\beta_{ji,m,K})\circ\bar\beta_{ji,-m,T_{i,m}K}=B_{ji}(\epsilon_{i,m,K}).$$
For the multiplication unitor $\lambda_i:B_{ii}\cong1$, the multiplication line datum gives $T_{i,m}(\lambda_{i,K})\bar\beta_{ii,m,K}=\lambda_{i,T_{i,m}K}$. More generally, if the source and target coefficient rings coincide but the prescribed line comparison is an arbitrary isomorphism, the scalar-unitor-normalized component is the termwise tensor map induced by that signed-power line isomorphism; it is not required to be identity. All these assertions include $m=0$ and negative $m$, and require neither completeness nor boundedness nor flatness of the ring maps.

proof.text:
Use the explicit $d$ of [lem-sfb-successive-derived-quotient-normalization]. On $(((p\otimes l)\otimes s)\otimes t)$ the left side of the tower equation is
$$(p\otimes r_{21}(s)t)\otimes b_{21,m}(b_{10,m}(l\otimes1)\otimes1),$$
whereas the right side is $(p\otimes r_{21}(s)t)\otimes b_{20,m}(l\otimes1)$. These are equal by the signed-power tower equation in [lem-pur-signed-line-scalar-tensor-tower]. Equality on generators gives equality of sheaf chain maps by [lem-pc-sites-sheaf-tensor-bilinear-universal], and Step 6 descends it. All intermediate representatives are flat-term K-flat by Steps 3--4, so this computation uses the specified $d$, without changing resolutions between the two paths. G5 implementation: ordinary_tower uses the composite ordinary adjunction to test the two maps on pure tensors. The supplied hom formulas, ordinary associator formula and signed-power tower equation identify these generators. Prolong this equality degreewise to cochain complexes. computation packages the canonical cochain computation maps as a natural transformation; compute_composition derives their tower square from Normalization.representative and the published quotientCompQhIso naturality. The proved categorical tower_on_representative pastes  these squares with the three Comparison.representative equations and cancels the invertible composite computation on a flat model. Finally natural_ext_on_good extends the equality to every derived object, using a flat-term K-flat resolution from lem-pc-kflat-resolution and naturality along its image isomorphism. This proves comparison_tower without using ordinary_line_derived_scalar_comparison or adding any unproved statements.

proof.text: For $r_{ii}=1$, the multiplication unitor on complexes is $p\otimes s\mapsto sp$ with inverse $p\mapsto p\otimes1$. By [lem-pur-signed-line-scalar-tensor-tower], multiplication line data give $b_{ii,m}(l\otimes1)=l$. Both sides of the required unit equation send $(p\otimes l)\otimes s$ to $sp\otimes l$, so agree as sheaf chain maps by [lem-pc-sites-sheaf-tensor-bilinear-universal], hence after localization by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property]. More generally let $a_m:M_{i,m}\cong M_{j,m}$ be the signed comparison over the identical ring. After inserting the inverse scalar unitor at the source and the scalar unitor at the target, the comparison sends $p\otimes l$ to $p\otimes a_m(l)$. Thus it is termwise tensor by $a_m$, not an imposed identity. The calculation uses no bound or completeness, and Steps 3--4 used no flatness of a coefficient map. The implemented exists_presentations obtains the scalar family from successive_derived_quotient_normalization. Adjoint uniqueness identifies identity scalar extension with the identity ordinary functor, using the normalized adjunction unit and scalar linearity. The universal derived counit and localization identify its derived functor with the identity; quotient comparison naturality gives the required computation formula. N1 implementation: comparison_identity specializes the arbitrary identity-ring comparison to A_m = identity, proves that the induced cochain map is identity degreewise, cancels the invertible factors and unitors, and applies Localization.natTrans_ext for the cochain quasi-isomorphism localization to get the equation on every derived object. J4 implementation: comparison_identity_arbitrary first proves the ordinary equation after multiplication normalization. Precompose with the inverse ordinary unitor; its value on a section x is the scalar section 1 tensor x. The prescribed comparison formula, the multiplication unitor formula, and the assumed equation for B_m reduce both sides to x tensor A_m(y). The existing sheaf tensor pure-generator extensionality proves the ordinary equation. Apply it degreewise to complexes. A generic categorical pasting calculation combines this equation with Comparison.representative, UnitData.computed and naturality of the two line factors and the derived unitor, proving the desired equality on flat-term K-flat complexes. For an arbitrary complex choose the quasi-isomorphism from a flat-term K-flat resolution supplied by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Both sides are components of natural transformations on the cochain category. Naturality for this quasi-isomorphism and cancellation of its invertible derived image extend the equation to the original complex. This does not require the original complex itself to be K-flat, and does not add any line-comparison or coefficient hypotheses. The already proved presentation/unitor construction is re-exported from OrdinaryLineScalarPresentations.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q148-5167bc23f (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item in full and its nine steps against every cited statement. The delivery is one commit with no new nodes, and the item is still unsplit in live and side-live with a verbatim statement. The only stmt_deps change is the added def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules, which the statement's 'flat-term K-flat' needs. There is no SGA citation and no cycle (closure of 264 nodes). Sources: Stacks 0G7E (sites-cohomology l.3508) and 07A4 (l.3684). The item's beta-bar is the 07A4 chain isomorphism for the identity topos with ring map r_ji, followed by b_ji,m. Blueprint: sk-def-sp-tate-twist-locally-free proof (3) is consistent. Step 1: local bases come from restriction commuting with tensor and Hom on slices; the contraction's local adjoint identifies M_-m with the dual of M_m for every sign of m. Step 2: the hypotheses of lem-pur-line-unbounded-derived-tensor are met, and it gives the exact evaluation formula. Step 3: K-flatness of P tensor M holds because tensor by M is a left adjoint and exact; terms are flat as composites of exact functors. Step 4: the K-flat pullback node applies with the identity topos and c=r_ji, needs no flatness of the ring map, and smallness comes from the proetale skeleton. Step 5: I rechecked the balancing relations and the inverse; the degree-0 factors give chain and homotopy compatibility. Step 6: both composites invert quasi-isomorphisms on the flat-term K-flat category, so gamma descends by the descent equivalence and the localization lemma (2) and (3). Steps 7-9: I recomputed the generators. The tower equation follows from the signed-line identity b02,m ass = b12,m(b01,m tensor 1), with indices transposed. The evaluation equation needs only commutativity. The unit clause holds, and an arbitrary datum gives tensor by a_m, not the identity. Edge cases checked: m=0, m=+-1, a unit u giving u^m (non-identity for u=-1), the non-flat map Z to Z/2, the zero ring, and unbounded K. Not duplicates of lem-pur-signed-line-derived-base-change (ring isomorphism under a topos morphism), lem-pur-signed-line-scalar-pullback-square (underived), the transport lemma (abstract, takes these equations as input) or lem-pur-line-unbounded-derived-tensor (fixed ring).
